Liquidity per position is capped by tickSpacingToMaxLiquidityPerTick (src/libraries/Pool.sol:166-171, :565-581), pool liquidity by uint128, and the step target is the next initialized tick inside one bitmap word or the price limit (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:85-122, src/libraries/Pool.sol:347-368).

The product needs a high price: with one position of maxLiquidityPerTick the step must start at tick 818,728 or above for spacing 1, 647,280 for spacing 60, 339,000 for spacing 1000 (out/bounds.json). There it is cheap. For spacing 1 the cheapest setup found is a pool of two ordinary tokens created by the account itself at tick 818728, one position [818728, 818984] of liquidity 191757530477355301479181766273477, which costs 4070057427382 units of currency0 and nothing of currency1 because the price sits at the lower tick. A swap of currency1 for currency0 with an exact input of 10^18 units then computes amountIn to the target as about 2^160 units at SwapMath.sol:68 and discards it at :69. A modifyLiquidity call that the PoolManager rejects reaches the same 512 bit branch with no tokens at all: the amount1 of a position below the price is computed at Pool.sol:229-236 and then fails toInt128. So the verifier's premise is wrong: the wide branch is open to any account on all 21 networks. Its conclusion still holds for the arithmetic, for a reason it did not give. On a successful call a wide amount1 is never settled. Where the step uses it (amountRemaining at least amountIn), the consumed amount is at least 2^160 and the cast at Pool.sol:452-458 reverts. Where the step discards it, it decides only the comparison at SwapMath.sol:69 or :91, against an amountRemaining below 2^127 for any call that can succeed, so a margin of at least 2^33 separates the two sides. Only a MULMOD answer wrong by a large amount could flip it. A wrong remainder at pc 22639 can do that: FullMath.sol:51-54 subtracts it from the product before the division, so a remainder near 2^256 gives a near-zero quotient. A wrong answer at pc 23094 (SqrtPriceMath.sol:252) changes amount1 by one unit of rounding at most.

cleared.result: pc 22585 (the mulmod by 2^256-1 at FullMath.sol:24), pc 22639 (the remainder at FullMath.sol:48, modulus 2^96) and pc 23094 (the rounding at SqrtPriceMath.sol:252, modulus 2^96) are the getAmount1Delta copy. Any account reaches them with an amountSpecified of -2^236 or below, which is a valid input: cases E (-2^250) and F (int256 minimum) succeed and stop at their price limits. Cycle 33's census shows pc 22513 never executed on MegaETH, and the list it gave left that pc out. Whatever MULMOD returns there cannot produce a wrong successful settlement. If amountRemainingLessFee came out at least amountIn, the step result would be the one on the specification. cleared.check: Task 2: live pools and whether any account can today make a swap step in an existing pool see a getAmount1Delta product of 2^256. Pools come from Initialize logs: the whole history on MegaETH (2 million block ranges) and HyperEVM (100,000 block ranges); on Monad, whose endpoints serve 100 blocks per query, the 34 pool keys in cycle 30's log dump since v0.16.7 and cycle 9's list. State was read by extsload of slot0, liquidity and the two bitmap words the first step searches (scripts/pools.py, refine.py, cost.py).
cleared.result: MegaETH: 143 pools; the largest product with existing in-range liquidity is 2^227; 22 pools could reach 2^256 with one added position of at most maxLiquidityPerTick that leaves the step target in place. All of these have tick spacing 9,900 to 19,998 and a step that runs to about tick 880,000. The cheapest such position needs 2^94 units of currency0, which is native ETH there (about 2e10 ETH), and 2^86 units of currency1. Every other one needs at least 2^91 units of one currency and up to 2^101 of the other. No holder can supply that. HyperEVM: 414 pools, largest product today 2^186, none reachable with one position (0). The two pools at tick 887,271 with zero liquidity cannot take an in-range position, because the largest usable tick of spacing 200 is below the price. Monad: 34 keyed pools, largest product 2^186, none reachable (0); the 109 pools seen only in Swap logs have no key and were not read. No existing pool of ordinary tokens offers the wide branch to a swap step. The cheap route of Task 1 is a pool the account creates itself, which holds no one else's liquidity.

cleared.check: Task 4 on Monad (L-1251): where Monad's execution at tag v0.16.7 clears transient storage between the transactions of a block.
cleared.result: Each transaction runs in a new State object over the block state, on the first attempt and on the retry after a failed merge (category/execution/ethereum/execute_transaction.cpp lines 458 and 484). Transient values live in AccountState::transient_storage_ (state3/account_state.hpp lines 70, 126-133, 151-154), which State builds from block_state_.read_account. That call returns only the account (state3/state.cpp lines 51-59, state2/block_state.cpp lines 58-77). BlockState::merge copies the account and storage_ of each touched address and never transient_storage_ (state2/block_state.cpp lines 194-235). A transaction therefore starts with empty transient storage, and CURRENCY_SLOT and RESERVES_OF_SLOT (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:11-13) read zero there. This is what EIP-1153 requires. The Monad endpoints rpc.monad.xyz and rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com (Monad/0.16.7) do not serve eth_simulateV1, and rpc2.monad.xyz (an erpc proxy) refuses it, so the live test did not run on Monad.

cleared.check: What a stale sync would do if a network failed to clear it, read from the source for Task 5.
cleared.result: sync needs no unlock and writes both slots together (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32). _settle reads the synced currency and credits balanceOf(this) minus the stored reserves, then resets the currency (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364). A stale value from another transaction would make a later settle credit the rise in the PoolManager's balance since that sync to whoever settles first, or revert a native settle with NonzeroNativeValue. On every build tested and read, the next transaction reads zero, so neither can happen there.

leads.question: The closed producers of MegaETH and HyperEVM have never executed pc 22639 (FullMath.sol:48 in the getAmount1Delta copy) with a product of 2^256 or more, or pc 22513 (the fee copy of SwapMath.sol:65) at all. Any account can make them do so with a pool it creates at tick 819,200 (spacing 1, one position of maxLiquidityPerTick costing about 4e12 units of currency0) or with amountSpecified of -2^236 or below. Does the MegaETH public validator re-execution or a HyperEVM replica disagree with a mined block that contains such a call? One would appear if anyone mines it. This review sends no transaction.
leads.why: A remainder at pc 22639 that is wrong by a large amount could flip the comparison at SwapMath.sol:69 and hand out the token0 of in-range liquidity for almost nothing. Replicas, interpreters and the Monad compiled-path model all return the reference word.

leadResults.answer: The critic is right that the wide branch is reached without transferring 2^160. Any account reaches it at every tick spacing with one position in a pool it creates at a high price, for about 4e12 units of currency0 at spacing 1, or with no tokens through a modifyLiquidity call the PoolManager rejects. No existing pool on MegaETH (143), HyperEVM (414) or Monad (34 keyed) offers it to a swap step: the largest product is 2^227, and the cheapest one-position setup needs 2^94 units of native ETH. On a successful call a wide amount never settles, because the SafeCast at Pool.sol:452-458 reverts on any use of it, and as a discarded value it decides only a comparison with a 2^33 margin. pcs 22585, 22639 and 23094, and the fee copy pcs 22445 and 22513, return the reference words on seven endpoints of the three networks. The closed producers remain unexercised and are listed as a lead.

Monad v0.16.7 builds a new State for each transaction, and BlockState::merge never copies transient_storage_ (execute_transaction.cpp 458 and 484, block_state.cpp 194-235). revm-context 18.0.3 under mega-evm 1.7.4 clears transient storage in commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize. A simulated block of sync(token), then exttload, then unlock and settle on the deployed PoolManager reads zero in the second and third transactions on MegaETH v2.2.1, HyperEVM b92ad36 and HyperEVM f0cad31, and the same-transaction control reads the token and its balance. No mined transaction on MegaETH or Monad ends with a sync open (cycle 33). Builds that refuse eth_simulateV1 were not tested live.
